name: Jehozabad
overview: Jehozabad was a male member of the tribe of Levi, specifically identified as the second-born son of Obed-edom. His place within the Levitical family highlights his role in the lineage associated with temple service and worship. Beyond his birth order and tribal affiliation, no additional notes elaborate on his life or actions.
namesAndTitles: The name Jehozabad means 'YHWH endows,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning tied to God's provision. This proper name was not given by God directly but is recorded in 1 Chronicles 26:4, emphasizing the divine blessing implied in his identity.
familyAndRelationships: Jehozabad is explicitly recorded as the son of Obed-edom, establishing his immediate family connection. Scripture does not provide further details about his family beyond this relationship.
scriptureSignificance: Jehozabad's significance in Scripture is primarily genealogical, as he represents a link in the Levitical lineage connected to temple duties. His identification as the second-born son of Obed-edom situates him within the sacred heritage responsible for worship and service in Israel. While the biblical text does not elaborate on his personal deeds, his mention preserves the continuity of the Levitical priesthood during the chronicled period.
